about.title: San Luis Obispo Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: When a crash on US-101, Los Osos Valley Road, or another San Luis Obispo corridor takes a life, the people left behind are often left with grief and unanswered questions at the same time. San Luis Obispo County recorded 179 injury collisions and one traffic death in the most recent final reporting year, a reminder that even a relatively small city carries real risk on its busiest streets, particularly on Friday afternoons when traffic tends to peak. California law allows certain surviving family members, starting with a spouse, domestic partner, or children, to pursue a wrongful death claim for their losses. Our team can explain standing, deadlines, and next steps, at no upfront cost. You focus on your family. We handle the legal work.

whyChoose.title: What Families in San Luis Obispo Should Know About Wrongful Death Law

items.title: Only Certain Family Members Have Standing
items.desc: California limits who can file a wrongful death claim, starting with a spouse, domestic partner, or children, and then certain other dependents or heirs. Our team can help identify who qualifies in your family's situation.

items.title: The Two-Year Clock Starts at Death
items.desc: California generally gives families two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death claim, though claims against a government agency involving a road defect may require action much sooner. Acting early preserves evidence and options.

items.title: Losses Include More Than Financial Costs
items.desc: Recoverable losses can include funeral and burial expenses and lost financial support, as well as non-economic losses like the loss of love, companionship, and guidance. Our team can help document these losses fully.

items.question: Who in our family is allowed to file a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: California law generally gives priority to a surviving spouse, domestic partner, and children. If none exist, other dependents or heirs may have standing depending on the circumstances. Our team can review your family's situation and explain who may bring the claim.

items.question: How long do we have to file after losing someone in a San Luis Obispo crash?
items.answer: In most cases, California allows two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death lawsuit. If the crash involved a government-owned road or vehicle, a much shorter notice deadline may apply. Because these deadlines are strict, it helps to speak with us as soon as you're able.

items.question: Does the location of the crash, like US-101 or Los Osos Valley Road, affect our claim?
items.answer: The location can matter for gathering evidence, such as traffic camera footage or witness accounts near known San Luis Obispo corridors, but it doesn't change who is eligible to file. Our team is familiar with local roads and reporting patterns, including the Friday afternoon peak in crash counts, and can use that context when building your case.

items.question: Is this a criminal case against the driver who caused the death?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a separate civil action focused on compensation for the surviving family, regardless of whether criminal charges are filed against the driver. The two processes can move on different timelines and don't depend on one another.
